screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled pilot RCT; evaluates intracervical nitroprusside gel for pain reduction; reports pain with IUD deployment (pain during insertion). Meets all criteria.
RCT, placebo‑controlled; intervention is ibuprofen 800 mg taken before IUD insertion; primary outcome is pain measured immediately after IUD insertion (pain during insertion).
RCT but primary outcome is ease of insertion; pain is reported only as a secondary, non‑specific overall score and no specific measurement at tenaculum, insertion, or up to 6 h.
RCT comparing intracervical lidocaine vs oral NSAID; pain assessed immediately after insertion and at 2 h and 6 h (pain after insertion up to 6 h).
Double‑blind RCT; ibuprofen vs placebo; reports pain at tenaculum placement, during insertion, and at 2 h/6 h post‑insertion.
Primary outcome is failed insertion; pain is a secondary outcome and not measured at the required time‑points (tenaculum, insertion, ≤6 h).
RCT; misoprostol vs placebo; pain recorded at tenaculum placement, insertion, and multiple post‑insertion time points; meets criteria.
Primary outcome is ease of insertion; pain reported only as a very general post‑procedure rating, not at tenaculum or within 6 h.
Large double‑blind RCT; ibuprofen vs placebo; primary outcome is pain after IUD insertion (pain during insertion).
RCT; misoprostol+diclofenac vs diclofenac alone; pain measured after insertion (within 6 h).
Double‑blind RCT; ibuprofen vs placebo; pain assessed during insertion and at several time points up to the third day (includes ≤6 h).
RCT with three arms (tramadol, naproxen, placebo); pain measured immediately after IUD insertion (primary endpoint).
RCT; misoprostol vs placebo; pain assessed at tenaculum placement, during insertion, and post‑insertion; meets criteria.
Double‑blind RCT; lidocaine gel vs placebo; pain measured at several procedural steps including insertion; primary outcome is pain.
Pilot RCT; nitroglycerin gel vs placebo; primary outcome pain with passage of IUD through cervix (pain during insertion).
RCT; paracervical block vs no anesthesia; pain recorded at tenaculum placement, insertion, and 5 min post‑procedure (within 6 h).
RCT with three arms (lidocaine gel, lubricant, no intervention); pain measured immediately after insertion (pain during insertion).
Double‑blind RCT; lidocaine infusion vs saline; pain assessed at tenaculum placement and during insertion (pain during insertion).
RCT; misoprostol+diclofenac vs diclofenac alone; pain measured on a VAS (1–10) during insertion (pain during insertion).
Double‑blind RCT; misoprostol vs placebo; primary outcomes include pain during insertion (≤6 h).
Intervention is aromatherapy; primary outcome is anxiety; pain is not a primary outcome nor measured at the required time‑points.
RCT; misoprostol vs placebo; pain recorded at tenaculum, during insertion, and post‑insertion (within 6 h).
Phase‑II RCT; lidocaine formulation vs placebo; primary outcome is pain during the first 10 minutes after insertion (pain during insertion).
Prospective controlled (single‑blind) study with three arms including paracervical block; pain recorded at tenaculum placement, insertion, and 5 min post‑procedure.
RCT; misoprostol vs placebo; primary outcome is pain at insertion (VAS 0–100 mm) and side‑effects; meets criteria.
RCT; lidocaine gel vs placebo; primary outcome is change in pain from baseline to insertion; also records tenaculum pain.
